precepts.text: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on. Like Bishop says, we know brothers fall on hard times. Come to the leadership, we will help you. But when it becomes a pattern with you, people are going to talk about you. Why are they talking? Because you do not have a job. You are always borrowing from this one, borrowing from that one. Here a little, there a little.
precepts.point: Now, we know brothers run on hard times. And very rarely will we not help a person in the body, if they hold a job and they pay their bills and they give offerings, they help. That is not how we move. But it should not be a side thing on the side. You lose the trust. When I hear that, what I think of is: we are back in the world.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
A quick precept on borrowing a little here and borrowing a little there: “Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on.” That is what was going on in Thessalonica. Some walked “disorderly, working not at all”, and they had become beggars by banqueting upon borrowing.

Paul had already commanded “that if any would not work, neither should he eat.” A man must labor. As a leader especially, you have to work and hold a job. How can you instruct the people and show them how to build a nation if the headman himself and the men under him are unemployed, refusing to work and take care of themselves?

“be talked on.” People are going to talk about your nasty bum self. Why are they talking? Because you are a bum. You don’t have a job. You are always borrowing from this one, borrowing from that one, here a little, there a little. That is why Paul says “note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed”: you are supposed to shame the man that refuses to work and is fleecing the people. Borrow here, borrow there, need this here, got this here.

We know brothers fall on hard times. Come to the leadership; we will help you. Very rarely will we not help a person in the body who holds a job, pays their bills, gives offerings and helps. That is not how we move. But when it becomes a pattern, and a side thing on the side, you lose the trust. When I hear that, what I think is: we are back in the world.

precepts.text: Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.
precepts.point: We had one brother just leave saying Captain Abiel kept putting too much pressure on him. What do you mean pressure? He is forcing me to go out and teach and do God's work, forcing me to be accountable. Spirits like that: just leave. Nobody is going to cry over spilled milk.
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” This is about self-examination, and it goes for all of us. “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”, so what was read about those men in Maccabees pertains to us even today, because there are men and women with those same hateful attributes.

The wise man says the same: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.” Examine yourself now, before judgment comes, and you will find mercy when the Lord visits.

What were those men's problems? Not sexual lust; nothing read that day was about a woman. It was covetousness: covetousness of power and authority, men wanting certain seats. From that came hatred, betrayal, a traitor, lies, theft, stealing from the temple, and murder. Everybody's demon is not the same. Covetousness is number ten of the commandments, but it is where all the others start, because it is internal, within you and me. Those are the sins to examine ourselves for.

One brother just left saying Captain Abiel kept putting too much pressure on him. What pressure? He is forcing me to go out and teach and do God's work, forcing me to be accountable. Are you kidding me? A spirit like that that will not examine itself, just leave. Nobody is going to cry over spilled milk. The one who examines himself before judgment finds mercy in the day of visitation.

precepts.text: A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time. That is integrity guiding you in every step: is this the right move, is this in alignment with the laws of God? In moments of correction, whether you can digest it and receive it is a sign of where your faith is at.
precepts.point: Captain's point: our integrity and our moral character are directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

So we have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord. That fear is “the root of wisdom”, and where it is present it drives away sin and “turneth away wrath.”

precepts.text: Before judgment examine thyself and find mercy in the day of visitation; humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins show repentance.
precepts.point: The Pharisees asked why Christ ate with publicans and sinners, the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18. They that be whole need not a physician: the law is not made for the righteous but for the sick, the lawless and whoremongers. I will have mercy and not sacrifice, from Hosea, and I am come to call sinners to repentance.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh humbled himself in his affliction, and the Lord saved him, unworthy as he was, “according to thy great mercy.” Sirach tells us to do it before the day comes: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.”

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the day of visitation you will find grace and mercy. “Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.”

Manasseh waited until he was bound in fetters in Babylon before he humbled himself. Don’t wait until you are sick, locked up, or exposed. In the time of wrong, show repentance, and the same mercy Manasseh found will be there for you.

precepts.text: Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites. Your appetite can be food, sex, the gym, TV, sports, or scrolling, whatever you overindulge in; today it is food and sex because if you get control over those two you can control anything. There are wants and needs: you need sex in marriage and food when hungry, then you choose what nourishes and gives energy to be productive. If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock. They post videos saying they cannot listen to a fat prophet, a brother bad to the bone in the street who cannot listen to himself, bring back fat-shaming. Satan tells you that you are hungry and to eat that McDonald's and that candy so you are sick every Sabbath and cannot do the work. Feed the body vitamins, fiber, and nutrients to possess the vessel.
precepts.point: Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats, but God shall destroy both it and them: you are arguing over food that God will destroy along with the one consuming it. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. He moves from food to fornication, the man with his father's wife from the previous chapter, because both are self-control over your vessel, created to be used for the master's work.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats”: food is for nourishment. “Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord”. Paul moves from food to fornication because the two are correlated: both deal with self-control over your vessel, which was created as a vessel of righteousness to be used for the master's work.

Sirach says: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” You might think it is only talking about sex, but your appetite can be anything you overindulge in: food, sex, working out, TV and entertainment, sports, scrolling. We focus on food and sex because they are one and the same, and if we get control over those two we can get control of anything in our life and reprogram our vessel to do what the Lord commands.

There are wants and there are needs. You need sex, in marriage; when you do not need, study, pray, fast. You are hungry, you eat and nourish your body, then you choose the foods that give you the energy to think, function and be productive in this work. That is what food is for.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” You become a laughingstock. There are videos saying, I can't listen to a fat prophet. A brother is powerful in the street, cutting people up, bad to the bone, and people say, I can't listen to you because you don't even listen to you. That is why they say bring back fat-shaming: you are operating outside the realm of discipline.

Satan tells you that you are hungry; Satan tells you to eat that McDonald's, that Burger King, that candy. These things are pushed on us to keep us sickly so we cannot do the work, sick every Sabbath. Feed the body the vitamins, fiber and nutrients it needs, so you possess your vessel and it serves the Lord.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, arrogancy, the evil way and the froward mouth.
precepts.point: Take heed of what is around you before you fall into sin.
precepts.why:
“A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence.” A wise man or woman, a brother or sister who applies the commandments, fears in everything. Why does he fear? What is the fear of the Lord? “The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.”

The fear of the Lord is to despise and loathe evil and everything that comes in the package with it. Pride is evil in the eyesight of the Lord, and a lot of us have a lot of it: you can’t tell me nothing, I’m older than you. Some sisters say, I want an older sister over me, not a younger one; brothers say, I want an older brother over me. That is pride. The Lord sent these people and put them in your life. Where someone over you has no children, leadership will pair you with someone who can help guide you with yours. You can learn from a baby; every day you wake up on this planet, you learn something.

Arrogancy: many of you cannot stand it when somebody corrects you for your own benefit. You get emotional and walk out the door: I know everything, you can’t tell me nothing. Then you are saying God can’t tell you nothing. Why are you here?

The froward mouth is that disrespectful, childlike, churlish mouth. A lot of you sisters are known for it with the new sisters coming in; some brothers are nasty too. New members come through the door and don’t want to come back because you are nasty. You have to soften, remove that man spirit, have a charitable spirit, kill that old man and that old woman. Christ said whoever offends one of his little ones, better a millstone be hanged about his neck. You have a judgment coming for that.

Does the Lord like those attributes? No: “do I hate.” So do a checkup from the neck up. Write it on the mirror: I deal with pride, arrogancy, an evil eye toward my brothers and sisters. Read your four chapters a day, because you will give account for yourself alone. That is the fear the wise man has, and why in the day of sinning he beware of offence.

precepts.text: Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites; David kept himself back from his iniquity all his days.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” David kept himself back from his iniquity all his days.

That is what he meant when he sang, “I was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity.” He refrained himself and held back his flesh, and the Lord recompensed him for it.
